title: Choose the visual world — July Uprising themed
question: The roll assigned Candlelight Vigil / Prodip Memorial — the museum's own subject as its visual world. Lock it, take the pick, or re-roll.

options.label: Candlelight Vigil (Prodip Memorial)
options.lineage: Bengali memorial vigil — clay prodip lamps lit for the dead
options.thesis: The archive holds vigil for its own subject: every clause lit like a lamp, not printed like a notice or sprayed like a slogan.
options.viewport: Full-bleed dusk-blue hero, glowing amber Bengali nameplate with soft bloom, a loose hand-scattered constellation of small lit-lamp icons above the title, six sections as individually glowing lamp-entries in an organic vigil arrangement, not a grid.
options.risk: Reads morose/heavy if the amber glow isn't kept warm and the layout stays too rigid — needs handmade variance, not a clean grid, to earn the vigil feeling.

raised.raise: Verification state renders as flame behavior — steady lit (verified), flickering (disputed), unlit wick (referred) — never a color swap, keeping the no-color-coded-judgment rule native to this world instead of borrowed.

options.label: Shaheed Minar Memorial Epigraphy
options.lineage: National martyr monument — official memorial register, stone/marble inscription
options.thesis: The archive reads like inscription on the monument itself — formal, permanent, carved.
options.risk: The most official, expected choice for a martyr-memorial museum — dignified but safe, and possibly too monumental/cold for a bilingual reading archive.
options.viewport: Stone-textured panels with carved-inscription headlines and formal wreath/laurel corner marks.

canonCard.label: Conventional Archive Page
canonCard.thesis: Plain neutral list of sections and clauses — the safe, unstyled category default.
canonCard.risk: This is what most AI-built archive sites already look like — the thing you asked to move away from.
